title: Health, Safety and Security at the Workplace
unit_name: Part B · Healthy, Safe and Secure Working Environment
short: Hazards, occupational health, electrical and fire safety, security of data.
lede: Unit 4 is definition-plus-example. Hazards and electrical safety are the core.
lens: **10 marks with the rest of Unit 4.** Hazard types + two precautions each.
Data security is part of this unit in the current curriculum — passwords, backups, authorised access.
concepts: **1. Hazard** = anything that can cause harm. **Risk** = chance that the harm will occur.
**2. Types of hazard:** physical (cables, noise, fire), electrical, chemical (cleaner fumes), biological, ergonomic (bad chair), psychosocial (stress, bullying).
**3. Occupational health:** physical and mental wellbeing at work. Fatigue, eye strain and RSI are IT-lab issues.
**4. Electrical safety:** no overloaded sockets, no frayed wires, dry hands, don’t open the SMPS, use earthed plugs, UPS/surge protector.
**5. Fire:** know exits, don’t block them, switch off power, use the **correct extinguisher** (CO2 / dry powder on electrical — not water).
**6. Security:** lock the lab, visitor register, don’t share passwords, lock the screen, authorised software only, backup.
**7. Policy / responsibility:** follow school/lab rules, report hazards, use equipment as trained. Employers provide a safe workplace; employees cooperate.
tricks: - Water on an electrical fire is the classic **wrong** answer.
- Hazard vs accident: hazard is the **potential**; accident is the **event**.
mistakes: - Writing “be careful” with no concrete precaution.
- Mixing this unit with the old “Web Applications and Security” syllabus.

qa.q: Differentiate a hazard and an accident with an IT-lab example.
qa.a: A **hazard** is a potential source of harm (a loose cable across the aisle). An **accident** is the event (a student trips and the monitor falls).

qa.q: List four electrical safety rules for a computer lab.
qa.a: Dry hands; earthed plugs; no overloaded boards; don’t open the power supply; report frayed wires; use a surge protector.

qa.q: Explain four types of workplace hazard with one IT-lab example each.
qa.a: Physical — trailing cables; electrical — open socket; ergonomic — low screen causing neck pain; psychosocial — long hours without a break. Control each: cable covers, close sockets, raise the monitor, timetable breaks.

qa.q: A student pours water on a sparking socket. Two mistakes and the correct actions.
qa.a: Water on electrical fire; staying next to a live spark. Instead: don’t touch, switch off mains if safe, alert staff, use CO2/powder extinguisher, evacuate.

title: Workplace Quality and Ergonomics
unit_name: Part B · Healthy, Safe and Secure Working Environment
short: Quality of work, 5S, housekeeping, ergonomic posture and workstation setup.
lede: Sit right, arrange the desk, and 5S the lab. This is the “quality measures” chapter.
lens: **Ergonomics of a computer workstation** is the set diagram/answer.
5S (Sort, Set in order, Shine, Standardise, Sustain) appears as a 2-mark list.
concepts: **1. Quality of work** in IT: accurate data, readable documents, meeting time, following the house style, checking before submit.
**2. Housekeeping:** clear aisles, labelled cables, no food, bags not in walkways, shut down PCs.
**3. 5S:** Sort (remove extra), Set in order (a place for everything), Shine (clean), Standardise (same method), Sustain (habit).
**4. Ergonomics** designs work to fit the person. Goal: reduce strain, errors and fatigue.
**5. Workstation:** feet flat, knees ~90°, back supported, screen top at eye level, screen an arm’s length away, elbows ~90°, mouse next to keyboard, wrists straight.
**6. 20-20-20 rule:** every 20 minutes look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds — reduces eye strain.
**7. Lighting and noise:** no glare on screen, enough light to read paper, headphones or quiet for data-entry accuracy.
tricks: - Screen **top at eye level**, not looking down at a laptop on the lap.
- 5S order is asked as a list — don’t shuffle Shine and Sort.
mistakes: - Drawing the user hunched over a laptop as “correct posture”.
- Defining quality as “working fast” with no accuracy.

qa.q: What is ergonomics? Give two workstation rules.
qa.a: Designing work to fit the person. Rules: screen at eye level, feet flat, back supported, wrists straight, mouse beside the keyboard.

qa.q: Expand 5S.
qa.a: Sort, Set in order, Shine, Standardise, Sustain.

qa.q: Describe a correct computer workstation and two quality checks before submitting a practical file.
qa.a: Chair and desk so elbows and knees are about 90°, screen arm’s length, top at eye level, no glare. Quality: proof-read, spell-check, file named as asked, print preview, backup copy.

qa.q: Amit’s laptop is on a high table, he looks up, and his wrists bend on the edge. Two injuries this invites and two fixes.
qa.a: Neck strain and wrist RSI. Fixes: raise the chair or lower the desk, laptop stand + external keyboard, wrist straight, breaks.

(b) Cable ties + labels; blinds or move screens; compulsory preview + peer check.
(c) Wrong data costs money and trust — the job role is Domestic Data Entry Operator.

title: Prevent Accidents and Emergencies
unit_name: Part B · Healthy, Safe and Secure Working Environment
short: Causes of accidents, evacuation, first aid, emergency numbers and incident reporting.
lede: Last chapter of IT 402. Evacuation steps and first aid for cuts, burns and shock.
lens: **Evacuation order** and **first aid don’ts** are the 2–3 markers.
Know: assembly point, don’t use lifts, report incidents even if small.
concepts: **1. Causes of accidents:** unsafe conditions (wet floor, bad wiring) and unsafe acts (running, bypassing rules). Most lab accidents are preventable.
**2. Prevention:** training, PPE where needed, maintenance, 5S, no horseplay, report near-misses.
**3. Emergency types:** fire, electric shock, medical, earthquake, data breach.
**4. Evacuation:** alarm → save work if safe and seconds allow → leave bags → nearest **stairs**, not lift → assembly point → headcount → don’t re-enter.

**5. First aid principles:** protect yourself, call for help, don’t move a seriously injured person, CPR only if trained, cool a burn with water (not ice/toothpaste), for shock switch off power **before** touching.
**6. Electric shock:** switch off mains, use a non-conductor to separate, call help, recovery position if breathing.
**7. Reporting:** date, time, place, names, what happened, injuries, witnesses, action taken. Near-misses count — they prevent the next accident.
**8. Numbers:** school office, local fire, ambulance 112 (India emergency). Keep them posted in the lab.
tricks: - **Power off before touch** is the electric-shock line examiners want.
- Near-miss reporting is a quality/safety behaviour, not “telling on someone”.
mistakes: - Applying toothpaste or ice directly on a burn.
- Using the lift during a fire drill.

qa.q: List four steps of evacuation in the correct order.
qa.a: Hear the alarm → leave via stairs (not lift) → go to the assembly point → answer the headcount and wait for the all-clear.

qa.q: Why report a near-miss?
qa.a: A near-miss shows a hazard that almost caused harm. Reporting it lets the school fix the condition before someone is actually injured.

qa.q: Explain first aid for (i) a small cut (ii) a minor burn (iii) suspected electric shock.
qa.a: Cut: wash, pressure, clean dressing. Burn: cool with running water 10 minutes, loose sterile cover, no toothpaste/ice. Shock: do not touch until power is off; then separate with a dry non-conductor, call help, monitor breathing.

qa.q: The fire alarm rings. A student runs back for a USB and takes the lift. Two wrong actions and the correct ones.
qa.a: Going back for belongings and using the lift. Correct: leave immediately by stairs, USB can be replaced, assemble for headcount.

qa.q:

(a) Immediate first actions.
(b) Why a report still matters.

(b) Near-miss/incident record → cable replaced, others warned, pattern spotted.
(c) Inspect peripherals, remove damaged devices, remind: report all shocks.
